rationale: Ground truth centers on: benchmark-harness architecture, missing profiling/VRAM evidence, and especially the native-speed-control/streaming-validation asymmetry (HTTP vs WebSocket) plus duration_factor bound duplication across talker/adapter/decoder. X finds a well-written but largely disjoint set of issues (uninitialized mel_head bias, S2Mel zero-audio fallback, IndexTTS-2 regression risk, payload-concat semantics) with almost no overlap with GT and no quoted source evidence to verify grounding. Y directly re-engages the same streaming/native-speed-control code path GT flagged (finding a related but distinct diffusion-dispatch bypass bug, plus a stale-docs contradiction matching linyueqian's ask) and backs nearly every claim with literal code quotes, making it easier to trust as grounded; it also surfaces a valid, independently useful CI-deselection bug. Both are highly actionable with file:line specificity, but Y's better topical overlap and stronger evidenced grounding give it the edge.
